Add a `type="pills"` variant to `st.tabs` to show tabs as pills

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a `type` parameter to `st.tabs` with a `"pills"` variant that renders the tab headers as pills (rounded, button-like segments) instead of the default underlined tab bar. Keep the same tab behavior — only the visual style of the tab headers changes.

### Why?

The underlined tab style is great for section navigation, but pill-style tabs are a very common, more compact and prominent look — especially for filters, view switchers, and dashboards. Today users approximate this with `st.pills`/`st.segmented_control` plus manual conditional rendering, which is more boilerplate and doesn't give the clean container-per-tab model that `st.tabs` provides.

### How?

Add a `type` parameter (default preserves today's look):

```python
tab1, tab2, tab3 = st.tabs(["Overview", "Details", "Settings"], type="pills")
with tab1:
    st.write("...")
```

- `type="default"` (or `"underline"`) — current tab bar.
- `type="pills"` — render the tab headers as pills.
- Everything else (content containers, active-tab state, etc.) stays identical.

### Additional Context

- Visually aligns `st.tabs` with the existing pill styling used by `st.pills` / `st.segmented_control`, but with the `st.tabs` container model.
- Design references for the pills style:
  - [Tailwind Plus — Tabs (pill variant)](https://tailwindcss.com/plus/ui-blocks/application-ui/navigation/tabs#component-2a66fc822e8ad55f59321825e5af0980)
  - [Tremor — Tabs, solid variant](https://tremor.so/docs/ui/tabs#example-tabs-solid-variant)
  - [Tremor — Tabs, stretched](https://tremor.so/docs/ui/tabs#example-streched-tabs)

گزارش کاربر حاوی درخواست اضافه کردن پارامتر type="pills" به st.tabs برای نمایش تب‌ها به شکل دکمه‌های rounded است. اما هیچ سند، نسخه فعلی یا نمونه کدی که این ویژگی را اثبات کند در داده‌های موجود مشاهده نشده است. پرسش درباره وجود مدرک کد یا نمونه عملی از ویژگی آن را تأیید یا رد می‌کند و به تصمیم‌گیری برای پاسخ یا ارجاع کمک می‌کند.

اطلاعات پیاده‌سازی و نسخه‌های آزمایشی آن مشخص نیست.
تابع st.tabs فقط تب‌های به سبک underline دارد و پارامتر type با مقدار "pills" در مستندات رسمی یا کد فعلی دیده نشده است.
اضافه‌شدن حالت نمایش قرص مانند به تب‌ها با افزودن پارامتر type="pills" به st.tabs بدون تغییر رفتار کلی تب‌ها.
امکان نمایش تب‌ها به شکل دکمه‌های rounded به صورت ساده و با مدل container-per-tab مشابه st.tabs نیاز است.

Add a `type="pills"` variant to `st.tabs` to show tabs as pills

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Add a `type` parameter to `st.tabs` with a `"pills"` variant that renders the tab headers as pills (rounded, button-like segments) instead of the default underlined tab bar. Keep the same tab behavior — only the visual style of the tab headers changes.

### Why?

The underlined tab style is great for section navigation, but pill-style tabs are a very common, more compact and prominent look — especially for filters, view switchers, and dashboards. Today users approximate this with `st.pills`/`st.segmented_control` plus manual conditional rendering, which is more boilerplate and doesn't give the clean container-per-tab model that `st.tabs` provides.

### How?

Add a `type` parameter (default preserves today's look):

```python
tab1, tab2, tab3 = st.tabs(["Overview", "Details", "Settings"], type="pills")
with tab1:
    st.write("...")
```

- `type="default"` (or `"underline"`) — current tab bar.
- `type="pills"` — render the tab headers as pills.
- Everything else (content containers, active-tab state, etc.) stays identical.

### Additional Context

- Visually aligns `st.tabs` with the existing pill styling used by `st.pills` / `st.segmented_control`, but with the `st.tabs` container model.
- Design references for the pills style:
  - [Tailwind Plus — Tabs (pill variant)](https://tailwindcss.com/plus/ui-blocks/application-ui/navigation/tabs#component-2a66fc822e8ad55f59321825e5af0980)
  - [Tremor — Tabs, solid variant](https://tremor.so/docs/ui/tabs#example-tabs-solid-variant)
  - [Tremor — Tabs, stretched](https://tremor.so/docs/ui/tabs#example-streched-tabs)

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open the app fresh in Safari (macOS or iOS) — a new tab/window, not a warm reload.
2. Before clicking anything, observe the st.pills widget with selection_mode="multi" and default=None.
3. All options render with the "selected" purple-outline styling, even though nothing has been selected yet.
4. The underlying state is correct (st.write(selected) shows an empty list) — this is a visual-only bug.
5. Does NOT reproduce in Chromium or in Playwright's WebKit engine — only in real Safari.

### Widgets are session dependent

Widget states are dependent on a particular session (browser connection). The actions of one user do not affect the widgets of any other user. Furthermore, if a user opens up multiple tabs to access an app, each tab will be a unique session. Changing a widget in one tab will not affect the same widget in another tab.

### Summary

When a fragment gets rerun and it has conditionally rendered child dialog (for example guarded by a button being clicked) the dialog will stop being responsive while still existing on the page

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st


@st.dialog("Dialog", dismissible=False)
def show_dialog() -> None:
    if st.button("Increment"):
        st.session_state["clicks"] = st.session_state.get("clicks", 0) + 1
    st.write("Clicks:", st.session_state.get("clicks", 0))


@st.fragment(run_every=5)
def parent_fragment() -> None:
    st.session_state["parent_runs"] = st.session_state.get("parent_runs", 0) + 1
    st.write("Parent runs:", st.session_state["parent_runs"])
    if st.button("Open dialog"):
        show_dialog()


st.write("Open the dialog, then wait for the parent fragment's next automatic rerun (every 5 seconds).")
parent_fragment()
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Click Open dialog
2. start clicking increment
3. after parent reruns the dialog stops being responsive and streamlit will log The fragment with id <id> does not exist anymore - it might have been removed during a preceding full-app rerun.

### Expected Behavior

The dialog to still be responsive

### Current Behavior

The dialog stops being responsive

- [x] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

- Streamlit version: 1.64.0
- Python version: Python 3.13.13
- Operating System: Linux 7.1.4-arch1-1
- Browser: Firefox

## Defining and calling a fragment

Streamlit provides a decorator ([`st.fragment`](/develop/api-reference/execution-flow/st.fragment)) to turn any function into a fragment function. When you call a fragment function that contains a widget function, a user triggers a _fragment rerun_ instead of a full rerun when they interact with that fragment's widget. During a fragment rerun, only your fragment function is re-executed. Anything within the main body of your fragment is updated on the frontend, while the rest of your app remains the same. We'll describe fragments written across multiple containers later on.

Here is a basic example of defining and calling a fragment function. Just like with caching, remember to call your function after defining it.

```python
import streamlit as st

@st.fragment
def fragment_function():
    if st.button("Hi!"):
        st.write("Hi back!")

fragment_function()
```

If you want the main body of your fragment to appear in the sidebar or another container, call your fragment function inside a context manager.

## Defining and calling a fragment

Streamlit provides a decorator ([`st.fragment`](/develop/api-reference/execution-flow/st.fragment)) to turn any function into a fragment function. When you call a fragment function that contains a widget function, a user triggers a _fragment rerun_ instead of a full rerun when they interact with that fragment's widget. During a fragment rerun, only your fragment function is re-executed. Anything within the main body of your fragment is updated on the frontend, while the rest of your app remains the same. We'll describe fragments written across multiple containers later on.

Here is a basic example of defining and calling a fragment function. Just like with caching, remember to call your function after defining it.

```python
import streamlit as st

@st.fragment
def fragment_function():
    if st.button("Hi!"):
        st.write("Hi back!")

fragment_function()
```

If you want the main body of your fragment to appear in the sidebar or another container, call your fragment function inside a context manager.

```python
with st.sidebar:
    fragment_function()
```
